contract: When primary load fails and a backup is used, store-level fallback recovery remains active.
An explicit session key absent from the backup is treated as ambiguous backup-missing-key, not fresh.
set() fails closed for such a key before provider/tool progress can be committed.
Explicit clear/reset is the deliberate operation that authorizes treating that missing key as fresh in the current process.
Normal clean-primary startup keeps new sessions working normally.

not_duplicate_of_current_workers: Qwen Core currently targets system-instruction preservation during stale-backup reconciliation of an existing recovered record.
Qwen Reliability currently targets provider/account persistence and qwen-client failure boundaries.
Notion Agent currently targets dynamic reservation/materialization and transport provenance.
Notion Core currently targets durable Responses replay ordering and native Windows gate.

limits: No production, real accounts, secrets, user data, or native Windows.
observed_gap: load() falls back to BACKUP_FILE and marks only keys present in that backup as recoveredFromBackupKeys.
A session created only in a newer primary can be completely absent from a stale backup.
getRecord(missing_key) then returns null even though the whole store is known to be in fallback-recovery mode.
server.js treats record=null as fresh state, so an explicit session id missing from the backup can reach provider work again.
If the missing newer session had already released a mutating tool call before the primary later corrupted, the same logical task can be replayed without QWEN_SESSION_RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN.
required_product_regression: backup without session-X; newer primary has accepted pending mutating tool call for session-X; backup refresh unavailable; primary later corrupts; restart from backup; request with explicit session-X must fail before provider with QWEN_SESSION_RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN.
same state + explicit reset(session-X) must allow a genuinely new session-X afterward.
clean first startup with readable empty primary must not classify arbitrary new session ids as recovery-uncertain.
